messages:
Maya S: Hey team, customer (acct 8421) is seeing 429s and large latency spikes during bursts. They reported it started after enabling cross-region failover. Stacktrace shows a lot of 429s coming from eu-west-1 despite original traffic being us-west-2. Can someone sanity-check routing/quotas?

Carlos R: which 429 are they seeing? service-level 429 or auth/plan limit?

Maya S: The response body is the standard rate limit: {"error":"rate_limited","message":"request rate exceeded"} and headers include x-rw-quota: 0/100 and x-rw-region: eu-west-1. Customer says their configured region is us-west-2 but we see cross-region routing after us-west-2 capacity hit.

Jun H: Do we have the request ids? need a trace id to follow through routing.

Maya S: Sent the example curl and response in DM earlier, but snippet here: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-***" \ "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'

Response headers:
x-rw-request-id: 0a9c2f6f
x-rw-region: eu-west-1
x-rw-quota: 0/100
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests

Also the customer pasted their dashboard showing spike at 2026-11-05T15:12Z and then automatic regional failover to eu-west-1.

Eli (SRE): ops-bot created INC-2026-45 for this. First pass: sounds like us-west-2 exhausted burst credits then smart-routing sent to eu-west-1 which either has no burst credits for this tenant or is enforcing per-region per-tenant quotas. We need to verify both region capacity and tenant quota windows.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-45 created and assigned to oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-45

Carlos R: Quick checklist I'll run: 1) confirm tenant quota config (global vs per-region), 2) check routing policy for cross-region (prefer-local? allow-fallback?), 3) check eu-west-1 capacity and if it's flagged degraded.

Jun H: Also want to repro locally. Maya, can you share the exact request pattern? burst size, rps, and if requests are pinned to a single key?

Maya S: Customer says they sent a burst of ~110 concurrent requests sustained for ~20s at t=15:12Z. They have reserved capacity in us-west-2 but those instances were full (they're on a reserved app tier with sticky affinity set to regional). The config looked like: 

\u003cconfig snippet\u003e
region: us-west-2
allow_fallback: true
affinity: region
reserved_capacity: 40 rps
burst_credits: auto
\u003c/end snippet\u003e

Eli (SRE): If reserved_capacity=40 but they sent 110 concurrent requests, fallback makes sense. But quota header showing 0/100 suggests eu-west has a tenant-level limit of 100 tokens and they'd hit it. Two possibilities: 1) cross-region quotas are independent and eu-west quota already used by another workload, 2) our fallback logic incorrectly prefers eu-west while other regions still had spare capacity.

Carlos R: I'm checking tenant config in provisioning: tenant 8421 has per-region quotas enabled, eu-west-1 limit 100 concurrent, us-west-2 limit 200. So fallback to eu-west should not have happened if us-west had capacity. Need to inspect routing decision logs for the request id 0a9c2f6f.

Jun H: On repro, I'll simulate with a load script that toggles allow_fallback flag. Sample test command: 

```bash
# hammer us-west then allow fallback
wrk -t4 -c120 -d20s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-..."
```

Eli (SRE): I pulled routing trace for 0a9c2f6f: decision tree: start->us-west-2 (capacity check returned 0 available slots at time T) -> fallback candidates list: [eu-west-1, asia-south-1] -> pick eu-west-1 (latency heuristic) -> enqueue -> eu-west returned 429 (quota_exceeded). The capacity check for us-west returned zero because of a transient de-schedule event of a dedicated pool node (OOM) at 15:11Z. Ops had autoscaler attempt to spin up, but spin-up took 18s. So requests in that window were eligible for fallback.

Maya S: So the summary is: us-west had transient capacity hole -> fallback allowed -> eu-west accepted some requests but throttled beyond 100 -> customer saw 429s.

Carlos R: Fix options: immediate for customer: 1) disable cross-region fallback (allow_fallback=false) so requests queue in us-west rather than failing in another region, 2) increase per-region quota in eu-west to accommodate fallback, 3) request reserved capacity top-up for their account in us-west. Which is customer-preferred?

Maya S: Customer prefers availability over strict regional affinity, but they don't want cross-region 429s. They asked for graceful failure to queue vs immediate 429 if fallback target is over quota. Can we make fallback check quota before routing?

Eli (SRE): We already do a pre-check but it's eventually consistent — quota snapshot can be stale in fallback window. Short-term workaround: change fallback policy to require both capacity_check && quota_check positive before routing. That requires a small routing change but can be gated. I'll open a PR for a conservative fallback policy flag: fallback_strict=true.

ops-bot: PR #5892 opened by Eli (SRE): https://git.redwood/pr/5892 - add fallback_strict flag to routing.

Carlos R: For the customer's incident, propose these action items: 1) set allow_fallback=false for tenant 8421 until routing fix deploys, 2) temporarily bump eu-west quota to 150 for tenant 8421 for 1 hour, 3) monitor for repeat during autoscaler events. Can ops do the bump?

Eli (SRE): I can apply the quota bump now. Doing: 

```bash
rw-admin tenant update 8421 --region eu-west-1 --concurrency-limit 150 --ttl 3600
```

Eli (SRE): Done. Quota now 150 for 1 hour. Also set allow_fallback=false for tenant 8421. 

Carlos R: I'll notify the customer with repro steps and temporary mitigations, and offer to schedule a call to discuss reserved capacity increases.

Maya S: Thanks. Customer confirmed they saw errors disappear after the bump and disabling fallback. They want a permanent fix.

Jun H: Follow-ups: 1) add stricter pre-check in routing (Eli PR), 2) improve visibility in console to show cross-region quota hits and fallback counts, 3) add a metric alert when fallback->target returns >=5% 429s in 5m window. I'll open tickets.

Eli (SRE): Creating follow-up tickets: RTE-324 (routing strict pre-check), OBS-776 (console quota visibility), ALERT-219 (fallback 429 alert).

ops-bot: Tickets created: RTE-324, OBS-776, ALERT-219.

Maya S: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Eli (SRE): leaving notes on the incident and will watch for regressions overnight.

Carlos R: adding postmortem blurb to the incident: root cause = transient dedicated pool node de-schedule causing capacity hole -> fallback exposed per-region quota mismatch -> customer-visible 429s. Remediation = routing pre-check + improved console + alerts + guidance for customers on fallback settings.

Maya S: Perfect. I'll mark the thread solved after customer ack.
